title: Focal Family
speaker: Haydn
script: A school vision letter identifies a concern. A family still has to arrange care and prepare the next conversation. Focal Family helps parents take that next step. We are seeking $600,000 to test family follow-through and build a product schools could buy, with free access for families.
sources: Team-selected product direction, October 30, 2026. Proposed investment terms and model.json.

title: Why we chose the school-letter moment
speaker: Fan
script: We started the semester testing three home vision-check ideas. Across five real interviews, the recurring barrier was arranging care: long waits, extra visits and uncertainty between exams. So we chose Family and a clear moment to act, a school vision letter. That use case is our proposal; interviews did not prove it. A randomized Michigan study of 162 children found documented eye exams within sixteen weeks for 65 percent with enhanced communication versus 48 percent with usual follow-up. That supports testing parent preparation, not Focal itself.
sources: docs/research/customer-discovery/interview-workbook.docx: five in-person interviews, one with a parent (Fan, My Mother). Recurring themes: appointment waits, inconvenient visits and uncertainty between exams. Exploratory context, not validation of school-referral demand.
https://headstart.gov/publication/vision-screening-referrals
Customer-discovery workbook: Parent Pat is a hypothetical persona, not an observed customer journey.

Musch et al., Journal of AAPOS 24(2), 2020, DOI 10.1016/j.jaapos.2019.12.012. Wayne County, Michigan, study conducted 2017; n=162; 52/80 versus 39/82 completed documented eye examinations within 16 weeks. This is external intervention evidence, not Focal performance.

The school-letter journey is illustrative; the real parent interview concerns scheduling and monitoring, not a demonstrated school-referral purchase need.

title: Parents use it. Schools are the proposed buyer
speaker: Fan
script: Parents of children aged four to ten use the free experience. A district student-services budget owner is our proposed purchaser; school nurses would champion and use the follow-up workflow. The annual site license would combine parent preparation with permitted status and staff reporting. That school product still needs building. We have five real interviews, including one parent, and five AI simulations. The budget source and willingness to pay must be tested with real school buyers.

docs/research/customer-discovery/presentation.pptx: slides 2 and 6
School buyer and purchasing case are proposed hypotheses.
The school license and reporting are proposed future deliverables, not existing customers or a deployed school-facing product.

title: Prepare the next conversation
speaker: Qingyi
script: The main output is a prepared parent conversation. A parent records observations, chooses a next step, and edits a note for the school nurse or eye doctor. Nothing is booked or sent. The optional direction task and history provide supporting activities; they do not decide whether a child needs care. A school referral still stands. This screenshot is a clearly labeled fictional example. We will now show the parent action first.
sources: https://focal-demo-b.streamlit.app/

Actual public-app screenshot captured November 4, 2026 after Explore a fictional example. The message contains the on-screen fictional-example label. No participant data, booking or message transmission.
Prototype B README and current public user interface. Task output does not establish clinical acuity.

title: Focal Family live demo
speaker: Qingyi 90 seconds, Burak 90 seconds
script:
Qingyi, first 90 seconds. Use two preloaded public-app tabs. Tab A: Parent activity, Explore a fictional example. At 0:00 identify the example as fictional, explain the school concern and parent-selected next step, and show the checklist. By 0:40 expand Add questions and prepare a message. Show a selected question, make one short demonstration edit to the draft, and point to the summary/message downloads without downloading on stage. Say that the parent decides what to share; nothing is sent or booked. At 1:30 hand over to Burak.

Burak, next 90 seconds. Tab B: Live vision check, physically prepared setup with practice completed before the talk. At 1:30 explain that the child points and the parent taps; demonstrate only one or two software-test responses. Do not finish or save a new check during this short demo. The purpose is to show the controls, not a clinical result. By 1:50 open Performance history, explicitly select Fictional example history and show one time window. Say the records are made up and cannot demonstrate eyesight improvement. At 2:30 return to Tab A's parent note. Close on the action: the parent has a next step and a message they control. School status and reporting remain funded work; the pilot will test family action and net staff effort. Return to slide 6 at 3:00.

Prepare both tabs before presenting and keep the fictional note/history distinct from software-test responses. If loading or navigation stalls for ten seconds, use slide 4's fictional note screenshot as the main fallback and slide 5's task screenshot only as supporting context. Do not spend the buffer troubleshooting. Finish within three minutes.
sources: https://focal-demo-b.streamlit.app/

Public Prototype B with Parent activity, Live vision check and Performance history, observed November 4, 2026. Two tabs keep the separate fictional parent-note example distinct from the live check. Preload and recheck before class. No switch to the master prototype is assumed.

Revised November 5, 2026: 90 seconds for parent preparation; 60 seconds for the optional task/history; 30 seconds returning to the parent action. No complete check, new save or file restore is required on stage.

title: The investment tests follow-through
speaker: Burak
script: Funding buys the school workflow and evidence of buyer value. Parent preparation already works; permitted school status and reporting need building. We will first test independent use and understanding, then run a proposed ten-site feasibility pilot against usual referral information. The decision gate is a fifteen-percentage-point improvement in completed next steps at thirty days, alongside measured net staff effort. Parent reports and verified actions stay separate. Clinical accuracy is a different question and is not established by this pilot.
sources: Prototype capabilities: prototypes/prototype-b-parent-guided-check/README.md
Pilot size, endpoints, and success gates are proposed targets. No completed pilot or signed customer is documented in the repo.
New testing/history modules demonstrate software behavior only. Clinical accuracy and repeatability are not established.

title: Our proposed advantage: easier follow-through
speaker: Fan
script: Letters and calls provide familiar contact. Our proposed addition is reusable parent preparation that could reduce repeated explanation. GoCheck Kids provides professional screening and clinical-record integration; Focal would complement it at home. Peek already has referral tracking, reminders and reporting. We therefore have to earn our place through easier parent completion and less net staff work. Those are advantages to test against existing workflows, not proven superiority or unique referral technology.

title: A school-first market worth testing
speaker: Haydn
script: The national benchmark is 52,450 public elementary schools in 2021-22. At the proposed annual price, that is $125.9 million. Our first outreach is in North Carolina. A pilot-fit site needs a referral workflow, a nurse champion and a district budget owner. We have not counted qualifying sites, so the $12.6 million subset remains an illustrative ten-percent allowance, not a measured market. The year-three target is 550 paid sites, or $1.32 million exit ARR.
sources: https://nces.ed.gov/programs/digest/d22/tables/dt22_216.10.asp : Elementary row, 2021-22, 52,450
model.json: $2,400 price, 10% serviceable assumption and 550 year-three sites. Market dollars are calculations, not published market-research estimates.
Eligibility criteria are proposed filters, not a measured count. The national 10% allowance is not the size of the North Carolina launch market.

title: How ten pilots could become fifty paid schools
speaker: Haydn
script: Here is the assumed path to fifty paying schools. Forty qualified district-buyer conversations lead to ten districts piloting one school each. If five districts buy an average of ten school licenses, we reach fifty sites by year-end. This assumes half the pilot districts convert and purchasing completes in time. We will test budget ownership and procurement early. There are no signed pilots or committed contracts in this funnel.
sources: Proposed go-to-market assumptions. No named institution or partnership is implied.
model.json: 50 paying sites at year-one end, net of cancellations.

Planning scenario: 40 district-buyer conversations; 10 districts with 1 pilot school each; 5 paying district contracts averaging 10 school sites = 50 year-end sites. 25% pilot entry and 50% pilot-district conversion are unvalidated assumptions. Districts license sites; site counts are net of cancellations.

title: $2,400 proposed annual school license
speaker: Hadley
script: Families use Focal free. Schools would pay $2,400 annually for preparation materials and, once built, permitted status and reporting. At an assumed forty dollars per staff hour, sixty net hours saved per school per year only covers the license. Value must exceed that threshold, including the work Focal adds. We will measure time per referred family and actual annual volume. Assumed direct costs remain $600 per site, leaving $1,800 gross profit and a 75 percent margin before operating expenses.
sources: model.json. All prices, costs, acquisition targets and staff-time values are illustrative planning assumptions. No insurance reimbursement or referral commissions are assumed.

School-specific materials, permitted status and staff reporting are the proposed paid offering; the school-facing status/reporting workflow is not built yet. No measured staff-time savings or school purchases are claimed.

Buyer value calculation: annual referred families × net staff minutes saved per family ÷ 60 × assumed $40/hour. Net time subtracts onboarding and added ongoing work. 60 net hours equals the $2,400 fee; adoption should require value above the fee. No measured savings are claimed.

title: A route to $1.32M in year-end ARR
speaker: Hadley
script: The forecast starts when funded. Year-end paying sites rise from fifty to two hundred fifty, then five hundred fifty. Recognized revenue is $42,000, $324,000 and $960,000. The $1.32 million headline is year-three exit ARR, not that year's revenue. COGS remains twenty-five percent of revenue. OPEX is $300,000, $450,000 and $660,000. Operating results are losses of $268,500 and $207,000, then a $60,000 surplus. The model is sensitive: a twenty-percent price cut makes year three a $132,000 loss. Adoption and timely collection are assumptions.
sources: model.json and calculated-model.json generated by build.mjs. Assumes linear site growth within half-years and collection in the same period. Excludes taxes, financing costs, capex and working-capital delays.

title: $600K funds the next 18 months
speaker: Hadley
script: The $600,000 raise funds eighteen months. We allocate $260,000 to product and research, $110,000 to pilots and sales, $60,000 to privacy and specialist review, $80,000 to administration and insurance, and $36,000 to delivery. That is $546,000 plus a $54,000 reserve. We test parent usability and buyer budgets first, then pilots and contracts, then paid expansion and renewals. Base-case receipts leave $198,000 cash. Hiring and rollout depend on paid demand and collection timing.
sources: model.json: sum of first three half-years. Use-of-funds total equals $600,000 including reserve. Renewal, clinical-content review and site targets are proposed work, not completed achievements.

title: Five owners for the next milestones
speaker: Qingyi 20 seconds, Burak 20 seconds
script:
Qingyi, 20 seconds: Our five-person team has built three product experiments. Haydn owns school access and fundraising, Fan customer evidence and messaging, and I own the parent experience and usability. Each investment milestone has a named owner.

Burak, 20 seconds: I own delivery, security implementation and integration. Hadley owns pricing and runway. We still need pediatric eye-care and school-health advisers. Our prototypes demonstrate execution; they do not establish clinical expertise.

The next eighteen months must show that parents complete follow-up actions, schools get value worth renewing, and delivery supports sustainable economics. The parent experience works today. Your investment would fund the evidence and school product needed to turn it into a business. Thank you.

title: Backup: the financial assumptions
speaker: Hadley
script: Revenue uses average active paying sites, not year-end sites. First half-year averages are 5, 30, 85, 185, 325 and 475. Each average site earns $1,200 for a six-month period and costs $300 to serve. Operating expenses are fully detailed in model.json. Site counts are net of cancellations, so gross wins must also replace losses. Working capital is simplified. The acquisition-cost target is $2,400 per site, which implies 16 months of gross-profit payback at $150 per month. A 90% annual retention target remains untested. At a 20% price cut, year-three revenue becomes $768,000 while direct delivery costs remain $240,000, giving a $132,000 operating loss after $660,000 OPEX. At 25% higher unit delivery cost, year-three COGS is $300,000 and operating result is zero. No clinical billing, referral fee or family subscription is in the base case.
sources: model.json. All forward-looking figures are illustrative, not actual results.

title: Backup: the pilot must earn a renewal
speaker: Fan and Qingyi
script:
Proposed first study: 10 school sites, approximately 200 consenting families, usual information versus usual information plus Focal, allocated within sites where feasible. Never withhold or delay a professional referral. This is a feasibility design, not a powered clinical efficacy trial. Agree the selected next-step definition, observation window and measurement plan before enrollment. Primary proposed outcome: a completed family-selected school contact or appointment-related action within 30 days, report parent statements separately from verified completion. Attendance at an examination is a separate endpoint. Compare staff time spent per family. Predefine exclusions and report missing follow-up. Proposed gates: at least 80% unaided workflow completion, 90% understanding that it is not screening, a 15-point uplift in next-step completion versus usual information, and willingness to renew at the proposed price. The 15-point gate is a business decision threshold, not an established effect. If families misunderstand the activity or the buyer sees no return, revise before scaling.

Buyer economics: record staff minutes per referred family under usual follow-up and with Focal, including onboarding and ongoing work. Annualize only using each school's actual annual referral volume. At an assumed $40/hour, 60 net hours saved per site per year covers only the $2,400 fee. The pilot's roughly 200 families are not an annual per-school volume assumption. Test value above the fee and a real paid renewal, rather than treating stated renewal intent as revenue.
sources: Prototype B README: original proposed usability criteria
New pilot proposal. Clinical and school partners must review study procedures before use.
Buyer-value threshold and $40/hour cost are proposed assumptions. No measured savings or paid renewal exists.

title: Backup: evidence and competitive limits
speaker: Fan
script: One real parent described preserving historical records and inconvenience around examinations. That supports studying preparation, not a universal unmet need or willingness to pay. Five AI interviews helped generate hypotheses and are not validation. No measured Family conversion, school pilot, paid customer or renewal result appears in the repo. Existing letters and calls are the baseline to beat. GoCheck Kids focuses on professional screening and integrated clinical records. Peek already offers a screening-to-treatment pathway and automated reminders; it cannot be dismissed as merely an acuity app. Focal's proposed parent-and-child preparation focus is a hypothesis about adoption and fit. None of these comparisons establishes superior clinical performance, lower cost or a defensible patent. We should partner or integrate where incumbents already perform well.

title: Backup: product boundaries and risks
speaker: Burak
script: The upgraded app records experimental direction-matching responses and retains saved checks in the current browser session. Families may download and restore a validated-format history file. There is no account, shared database, camera, prescription, diagnosis, booking or automatic message sending. The 20/x labels describe symbol geometry, not measured acuity. Same-setup comparisons avoid combining different children, eyes, correction, distance or reference widths. Attention, learning, guessing and self-reported setup still limit interpretation. This app must never clear a child from a professional referral. Production partner reporting needs appropriate permissions, secure storage, access control and expert review. Usability, clinical accuracy, school demand and renewal are separate questions that we must test before expanding claims.
